title: Specify the uniqueness-point information convention before held-out historical-text comparison
statement: In 30,000-token public samples of ZL and IT, and in three nonoverlapping 30,000-token windows each from four historical comparison texts, each word-length group 4–8 shows a positive type-level slope of relative uniqueness position against log word frequency and a negative slope of finite pre-uniqueness segment information against log frequency. These are related to the published directions but are not an exact reproduction: the printed leave-one-word-out formula is undefined at a unique prefix, and the paper does not specify how that term enters its mean.
check: Obtain or independently specify the treatment of the zero numerator at the uniqueness point, word-boundary-only uniqueness, type versus token weighting, segment units, text inclusion and word length. Validate an approved measurement primitive against hand-computed prefix trees and the published implementation if available. Register fixed comparison directions and minimum samples before the manuscript held-out run; compare independent transcription witnesses and size-matched historical references, accounting for shared word-type and corpus dependence. Include a structured non-language generator, not merely token-frequency shuffles.
method: Use the first 30,000 certain ASCII lowercase word tokens from public practice-training pages in each of ZL3b and IT2a, all transcription line units, original raw EVA character spelling (not eva-basic segmentation). For each of Dante, Libro de Buen Amor, the Paston Letters and Jan Hus’s 1413 Postilla, use three consecutive nonoverlapping 30,000-token windows of the project’s normalized pinned transcription; the eras refer to underlying works and some editions are later. Verify all source hashes. Count distinct word types and token-weighted counts of every prefix. For a type, its uniqueness point is the first prefix occurring in exactly one type; if it is a prefix of another type, use an end-of-word point at length+1. Relative position divides by the character length, hence can exceed 1. For each character before the uniqueness point, compute minus log2 of (prefix-token count minus the type’s count) divided by (previous-prefix-token count minus the type’s count), then average finite values. The uniqueness-point character is excluded because the printed leave-one-out numerator is zero; types with no finite terms are omitted from that information regression and counted. For each length 4–8, regress each outcome separately on log2(type frequency / 30,000), giving each type equal weight. The 49 seeded controls permute type counts within each word length, rebuild the prefix counts and repeat the regressions. Directional tails are greater for uniqueness slopes and less for information slopes, with add-one correction.
source: Colin Layfield, Lonneke van der Plas, Michael Rosner and John Abela, Word Probability Findings in the Voynich Manuscript (2020), https://aclanthology.org/2020.lt4hala-1.11/ ; zero-numerator convention is this pilot’s explicit choice, not an attributed author decision.

reproduce.instructions: Save script as /tmp/voy_k041_probability.py. Run python3 -m vs fetch to obtain the pinned data and then PYTHONPATH=. python3 /tmp/voy_k041_probability.py from repository root; the script verifies both transcription and historical source hashes.

validation: A separate brute-force implementation that scans every type for each prefix agreed with the prefix-counter regressions on five seeded random synthetic lexicons. The lower-tail and upper-tail shuffle directions were checked against the stated hypothesis.
limitations: The leave-one-word-out value at a unique prefix is mathematically undefined; averaging only the earlier finite segments is an explicit interpretation, not a confirmed match for the paper’s code. Mean information, UP length, vocabulary and frequency are calculated on the same sample; types share prefixes and are not independent. ZL and IT are witnesses of the same manuscript, not independent samples. The three windows within each comparison book are not independent books and later editions may normalize historical orthography. Fixed 49 permutations yield minimum p=.02 and no multiple-comparison correction; their output is exploratory and does not establish specificity against structured meaningless text. A public practice-training sample is not the secret held-out verdict. The current trusted DSL does not implement these statistics.
